title: Common Problems
markdown:
| Problem | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every socket call fails with `WSANOTINITIALISED` | `WSAStartup` was never called | call it once at the start of the program | 2.01 |
| Messages arrive merged or cut in pieces | TCP is a byte stream with no boundaries | frame messages (length prefix or delimiter) and loop on `recv` | 2.02 |
| Only part of the data is sent | `send` may accept fewer bytes than asked | loop until every byte is sent | 2.02 |
| Numbers arrive scrambled | host byte order on the wire | convert with `htons`/`htonl` and back with `ntohs`/`ntohl` | 2.03 |
| `connect` fails with `WSAECONNREFUSED` | nothing is listening on that address and port | start the server; check the port and the address it bound to | 2.01 |
| The server works locally but not from another machine | bound to `127.0.0.1`, or blocked by the firewall | bind to `0.0.0.0` (or the right interface) and allow the port | 2.02 |
| `bind` fails with `WSAEADDRINUSE` | another program, or a previous run, holds the port | stop it or choose another port | 2.02 |
| One slow client freezes the whole server | blocking calls on one thread | `select`/`WSAPoll`, non-blocking sockets or a thread per client | 2.04 |
| UDP requests sometimes get no answer | the datagram or its reply was lost | time out and retry, with a limit | 2.05 |
| The HTTP response never ends | missing or wrong `Content-Length` | send the exact body length, or close the connection | 3.01 |
| A server is crashed by one huge request | no limit on head or body size | enforce limits; reply 431 or 413 | 3.02 |
| A path like `../../secret` escapes the web folder | the URL path is used as a file path unchecked | decode, normalise and reject `..` | 3.04 |
| Certificate errors on HTTPS | hostname mismatch, expired or untrusted certificate | fix the certificate; never turn verification off | 3.05 |
| No packets appear for `127.0.0.1` in Wireshark | loopback traffic does not touch the network card | capture on the Npcap loopback adapter | 4.01 |
| Wireshark shows bad TCP checksums on outgoing packets | checksum offloading to the network card | expected; disable checksum validation | 4.03 |
| A decoder reads garbage after the IP header | assumed a 20-byte header, or treated a fragment as having TCP | use IHL × 4 and check the fragment offset | 4.02 |
| A game freezes briefly whenever packets are lost | TCP's head-of-line blocking | use UDP and resend only what must arrive | 5.01 |
| Old packets are treated as new after a while | sequence numbers compared with plain `<` | use the wrapping difference | 5.02 |
| A connection floods the network when it breaks | resending at a fixed rate | exponential backoff | 5.04 |
| Large UDP messages are lost far more often | IP fragmentation | keep datagrams under about 1 200 bytes and fragment yourself | 5.05 |
| Remote players stutter or jump | showing the newest snapshot directly | interpolate a little in the past | 6.03 |
| Your own movement feels delayed | waiting for the server | client-side prediction | 6.04 |
| Your player jitters constantly | client and server simulation differ | share the exact movement code and quantisation | 6.04 |
| Shots that clearly hit on screen miss | the server tests against current positions | lag compensation | 6.05 |
